operations.description: List the calendars on the signed-in user's calendar list, one page per call; the walk follows nextPageToken as pageToken and ends on the page carrying nextSyncToken, which a later call sends as syncToken to read only the entries changed since; a 410 (not_found) means the sync token expired: drop it and walk again without it

List the events of calendarId (primary for the signed-in user's own), one page per call, optionally within timeMin..timeMax or changed after updatedMin, with singleEvents to expand recurring events and eventTypes (an array) to select types; the walk follows nextPageToken as pageToken and ends on the page carrying nextSyncToken, which a later call sends as syncToken, without timeMin, timeMax, updatedMin, q, orderBy, iCalUID or the extended-property filters, to read only the events changed since; a 410 (not_found) means the sync token expired: drop it and walk again without it
Read one event by calendarId and eventId

Create one event on calendarId (primary for the signed-in user's own) from body, a Calendar Event resource. Unguarded: nothing exists to compare before a create, so the same input approved and sent again makes a second event; a body.id must be unique per calendar, but the pinned document says Google cannot guarantee to detect a collision at creation, so an id does not make a repeated create safe. Every guest in body.attendees is invited, and sendUpdates, which is required and must be all, externalOnly or none (the provider does not check the value, so check it before approving), decides whom Google emails; the pinned document says some emails might still be sent and that none can leave external calendars out of sync, so name it explicitly. Among other effects: with conferenceDataVersion 1, body.conferenceData.createRequest creates a new conference, such as a Google Meet link, on the event; body.guestsCanModify lets guests change the event, and body.guestsCanInviteOthers and body.guestsCanSeeOtherGuests default to true, so guests may invite others and see each other unless the body says otherwise; body.visibility public shows its details to every reader of the calendar; body.recurrence makes it a recurring series; an outOfOffice or focusTime event whose body.outOfOfficeProperties or body.focusTimeProperties sets an autoDeclineMode other than declineNone declines conflicting meeting invitations; body.attachments needs supportsAttachments; sent with maxAttendees, the answer lists only the participant. This list is not exhaustive: the approval binds the whole input by digest, so read the whole input before approving

Change one confirmed event by calendarId and eventId while its etag is the pinned etag, read from events.get or events.list; the provider reads the event first and refuses before any write when its etag differs or its status is not confirmed, so a cancelled (deleted) or tentative event is refused, and a change between that read and the patch is not detected. Each field given in body replaces the stored one: body.attendees replaces the whole guest list, so a guest left out is removed and a guest added is invited; an event read or written with maxAttendees lists only the participant and sets attendeesOmitted; a body copied from such an answer carries attendeesOmitted true, which the pinned document says limits an update to the participant's response, and what Google does with a truncated guest list is not verified: read the event without maxAttendees before patching attendees. sendUpdates, which is required and must be all, externalOnly or none (the provider does not check the value, so check it before approving), decides whom Google emails about the change; name it explicitly. The id of a recurring event changes the series and so every instance of it. Among other effects: with conferenceDataVersion 1, body.conferenceData.createRequest creates a new conference on the event; body.guestsCanModify, body.guestsCanInviteOthers and body.guestsCanSeeOtherGuests change what guests may do and see; body.visibility changes who sees its details; body.recurrence changes the series. This list is not exhaustive: the approval binds the whole input by digest, so read the whole input before approving

Delete one confirmed event by calendarId and eventId while its etag is the pinned etag, read from events.get or events.list; the provider reads the event first and refuses before any write when its etag differs or its status is not confirmed, so a cancelled (deleted) or tentative event is refused, and a change between that read and the delete is not detected. The id of a recurring event deletes the series and so every instance of it; an instance's own id deletes that instance. sendUpdates, which is required and must be all, externalOnly or none (the provider does not check the value, so check it before approving), decides whom Google emails a cancellation; name it explicitly. Google answers with an empty body, returned as a null body. The approval binds the whole input by digest, so read the whole input before approving
